To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Sun is enriched in the elements Sc, V, Co and Ni, but depleted in the elements Ti, Mn and Zn.

the solar abundances of C, O, Mg, Si, S, Ar, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn and Ni are in good agreement with meteoritic abundances, but that the abundances of N, Na, Al, K, Sc and V are significantly lower than meteoritic values.

the solar photospheric iron abundance is 7.47±0.04 (dex), that there is no evidence that the iron abundance varies with depth in the solar photosphere and that there are no systematic trends with atomic number for iron group elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
determining the elemental abundances of the Sun with the highest precision possible.
the elemental composition of the photosphere of the Sun.
determining the chemical composition of the Sun.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no significant discrepancies between the new solar abundances and the meteoritic ones, except for a few individual cases, such as the C and O abundances.
the solar iron peak elements are not significantly overabundant compared to CI meteorites, but there are some notable exceptions.
the Sun is indeed metal poor compared to the meteorites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we find a solar Fe/H abundance of 7.51 ± 0.03 (log) and a total solar iron mass of 1.9 × 10 ^{27} kg.
the abundances of most elements are now known to better than 0.1 dex, but for a few key elements, the uncertainties still remain at the 0.2-0.3 dex level.
our solar iron group abundances are consistent with the CI meteorite abundances, with the notable exceptions of Sc and V.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no evidence for a large discrepancy between the solar and the meteoritic iron group abundances, and that the Sun is indeed a typical star in this respect.
the solar abundances of the iron group elements do not differ significantly from the meteoritic ones.
the solar abundances of the iron group elements are generally consistent with the CI meteorite abundances, and that the 3D NLTE corrections to the abundances are small.
